$comment: linux-arm64 and win32-arm64 are pinned but their checksums are not recorded yet: nobody has downloaded
those two archives to hash them, and neither is in the release matrix. Run --record on them before
ffmpeg and ffprobe, pinned per platform. These ship inside the installer, unlike yt-dlp (ADR 0010).
The Dockerfile fetches `latest` and that is fine for a self-hoster building an image on their own
machine; it is not fine for a binary you sign and hand to other people, so every entry here names
one immutable build and the SHA-256 its archive must have. A mismatch fails the fetch.
Always the `gpl` build variant, never `lgpl`: BtbN's own build scripts (scripts.d/50-rubberband.sh)
strip librubberband out of every lgpl* variant, and Rubber Band is this app's only pitch and tempo
engine — the Dockerfile carries the long version of this reasoning, and ADR 0004 already commits the
whole project to GPL-3.0 because of it. The macOS build is compiled from source instead, with rubberband
linked in and checked for before it is installed (see the darwin-arm64 entry).
A null sha256 means nobody has verified that build yet, and `fetch-binaries.ts` refuses it. Run it
with --record on a machine that can reach the URL to fill one in.

win32-x64.$verified: Downloaded and checked: `ffmpeg -version` reports --enable-gpl and --enable-librubberband, and `ffmpeg -filters` lists the rubberband filter.

linux-x64.$verified: Downloaded and hashed. Not run — the machine that pinned it was Windows. Same BtbN build matrix and same `gpl` variant as win32-x64, whose `ffmpeg -version` was checked and reports --enable-librubberband.

darwin-arm64.$comment: Built, not downloaded. No publisher ships a static Apple Silicon ffmpeg with librubberband: evermeet.cx is x64-only, and martin-riedl.de and osxexperts.net (which ffmpeg-static repackages) both leave rubberband out. scripts/build-ffmpeg-darwin-arm64.sh compiles ffmpeg, Rubber Band, and LAME from source tarballs pinned by SHA-256, links both libraries statically, and refuses to install a binary that is not arm64-only, links anything outside macOS itself, or lacks the rubberband filter or libmp3lame. There is no Intel macOS build: macOS means Apple Silicon for this app.
